claim: Inflammation is currently recognized as one of the major causes of premature delivery.
source: Inflammation is currently recognized as one of the major causes of premature delivery.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction and abstract, supported by the broader scientific literature on preterm labor.

claim: IL-33 is a member of the interleukin-1β (IL-1β) family.
source: As a member of the interleukin-1β (IL-1β) family, interleukin-33 (IL-33) has been shown to be involved in normal pregnancy as well as a variety of pregnancy-related disorder.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and represents established scientific knowledge about IL-33 classification.

claim: IL-33 has been shown to be involved in normal pregnancy as well as a variety of pregnancy-related disorders.
source: As a member of the interleukin-1β (IL-1β) family, interleukin-33 (IL-33) has been shown to be involved in normal pregnancy as well as a variety of pregnancy-related disorder.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research in the field.

claim: LPS reduced the expression of nuclear IL-33 in a time-limited manner.
source: LPS reduced the expression of nuclear IL-33 in a time-limited manner and induced ER stress.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 demonstrating time-dependent changes in nuclear IL-33 after LPS treatment.

claim: LPS induced ER stress in myometrial cells.
source: LPS reduced the expression of nuclear IL-33 in a time-limited manner and induced ER stress.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data showing increased ER stress markers (p-IRE1α, XBP1s) after LPS treatment.

claim: Knockdown of IL-33 increased LPS-induced calcium concentration.
source: However, knockdown of IL-33 increased LPS-induced calcium concentration, ER stress and phosphorylation of nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB), and P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Knockdown of IL-33 increased LPS-induced ER stress.
source: However, knockdown of IL-33 increased LPS-induced calcium concentration, ER stress and phosphorylation of nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB), and P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 5D showing increased p-IRE1α and XBP1s in IL-33 siRNA treated cells.

claim: Knockdown of IL-33 increased phosphorylation of NF-κB.
source: However, knockdown of IL-33 increased LPS-induced calcium concentration, ER stress and phosphorylation of nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB), and P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 7B showing increased p-NF-κB in IL-33 siRNA treated cells.

claim: Knockdown of IL-33 increased phosphorylation of P38 MAPK.
source: However, knockdown of IL-33 increased LPS-induced calcium concentration, ER stress and phosphorylation of nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB), and P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 7B showing increased p-P38 in IL-33 siRNA treated cells.

claim: siRNA IL-33 further stimulates LPS enhanced cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression via NF-κB and p38 pathways.
source: In addition, siRNA IL-33 further stimulates LPS enhanced cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression via NF-κB and p38 pathways.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figures 6A and 7 showing increased COX-2 expression with IL-33 knockdown and reduction with pathway inhibitors.

claim: IL-33 expression was decreased in the nucleus with the onset of labor.
source: IL-33 expression was decreased in the nucleus with the onset of labor.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and western blot data in Figure 1 comparing labor and nonlabor groups.

claim: LPS-induced ER stress in cultured myometrial cells.
source: LPS-induced ER stress and increased expression of the labor-associated gene, COX-2, as well as IL-6 and IL-8 in cultured myometrial cells.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data showing increased ER stress markers after LPS treatment.

claim: LPS increased expression of COX-2 in cultured myometrial cells.
source: LPS-induced ER stress and increased expression of the labor-associated gene, COX-2, as well as IL-6 and IL-8 in cultured myometrial cells.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in multiple figures showing increased COX-2 protein after LPS treatment.

claim: LPS increased expression of IL-6 in cultured myometrial cells.
source: LPS-induced ER stress and increased expression of the labor-associated gene, COX-2, as well as IL-6 and IL-8 in cultured myometrial cells.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data in Figure 8 showing increased IL-6 secretion after LPS treatment.

claim: LPS increased expression of IL-8 in cultured myometrial cells.
source: LPS-induced ER stress and increased expression of the labor-associated gene, COX-2, as well as IL-6 and IL-8 in cultured myometrial cells.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data in Figure 8 showing increased IL-8 secretion after LPS treatment.

claim: After IL-33 was knocked down, the stimulating effect of LPS on calcium was enhanced.
source: IL-33 also increased COX-2 expression, but after it was knocked down, the stimulating effect of LPS on calcium was enhanced.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3A showing increased calcium fluorescence in IL-33 siRNA treated cells.

claim: 4μ8C inhibited the expression of COX-2 markedly.
source: 4μ8C also inhibited the expression of COX-2 markedly.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 6B showing reduced COX-2 expression with 4μ8C treatment.

claim: The expression of calcium channels on the membrane was increased with IL-33 knockdown and LPS treatment.
source: The expression of calcium channels on the membrane and intracellular free calcium ion were both increased which was accompanied by phosphorylated NF-κB and p38.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 3B showing increased Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 expression.

claim: Intracellular free calcium ion was increased with IL-33 knockdown and LPS treatment.
source: The expression of calcium channels on the membrane and intracellular free calcium ion were both increased which was accompanied by phosphorylated NF-κB and p38.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3A showing increased calcium fluorescence.

claim: IL-33 may be involved in the initiation of labor by leading to stress of the ER via an influx of calcium ions in human uterine smooth muscle cells.
source: These data suggest that IL-33 may be involved in the initiation of labor by leading to stress of the ER via an influx of calcium ions in human uterine smooth muscle cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing relationships between IL-33, calcium, ER stress, and labor markers.

claim: Preterm delivery occurs before 37 weeks of gestation.
source: Preterm delivery occurs before 37 weeks of gestation and is one of the major causes of perinatal morbidity and mortality.
evidence: This is a standard clinical definition in obstetrics.

claim: Preterm delivery is one of the major causes of perinatal morbidity and mortality.
source: Preterm delivery occurs before 37 weeks of gestation and is one of the major causes of perinatal morbidity and mortality.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about the clinical significance of preterm birth.

claim: Infection, uterine over-distension, decline in progesterone action, breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance, stress, and other unknown reasons are involved in PTL.
source: It is widely accepted that infection, uterine over-distension, decline in progesterone action, breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance, stress, and other unknown reasons are involved in PTL (Romero et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Romero et al., 2014 and represents current understanding in the field.

claim: All of the reasons for PTL lead to inflammatory events.
source: However, all of these reasons lead to inflammatory events.
evidence: This is an inference based on the literature and the common pathway hypothesis for preterm labor.

claim: Inflammatory events in PTL are mainly due to the identification of microorganisms and their products, and increased secretion of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines in the decidua and myometrium.
source: These are mainly due to the identification of microorganisms and their products, and increased secretion of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines in the decidua and myometrium, which enable leukocytes to infiltrate the uterus leading to its activation (Goldenberg et al., 2008; Lamont, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goldenberg et al., 2008 and Lamont, 2015.

claim: IL-1β is one of the well-recognized inflammatory factors that induce the initiation of labor.
source: As a member of IL-1 family, IL-1β is one of the well-recognized inflammatory factors that induce the initiation of labor.
evidence: This represents established knowledge in the field of parturition research.

claim: IL-33 is expressed in a variety of cells, including innate immune (macrophage and dendritic), Th2, B, epithelial, endothelial, and muscle cells.
source: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is another member of the IL-1 family and it is expressed in a variety of cells, including innate immune (macrophage and dendritic), Th2, B, epithelial, endothelial, and muscle cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IL-33 expression patterns.

claim: IL-33 has been shown to have a key role in various diseases, including inflammation-associated autoimmune (including asthma), cardiovascular, and allergic diseases.
source: Also, it has been shown to have a key role in various diseases, including inflammation-associated autoimmune (including asthma), cardiovascular, and allergic diseases (Cayrol and Girard, 2018; Drake and Kita, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cayrol and Girard, 2018 and Drake and Kita, 2017.

claim: After exogenous administration of IL-33, it was able to activate B cell-mediated immune regulation and promote the expression of progesterone-induced blocking factor 1 (PIBF1).
source: Recently, Huang et al., 2017 found that after exogenous administration of IL-33, it was able to activate B cell-mediated immune regulation and promote the expression of progesterone-induced blocking factor 1 (PIBF1), which plays an essential role in safeguarding against PTL.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2017.

claim: PIBF1 plays an essential role in safeguarding against PTL.
source: Recently, Huang et al., 2017 found that after exogenous administration of IL-33, it was able to activate B cell-mediated immune regulation and promote the expression of progesterone-induced blocking factor 1 (PIBF1), which plays an essential role in safeguarding against PTL.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2017.

claim: IL-33 was mainly located in the nuclei of myometrial cells.
source: Preliminary data showed that IL-33 was mainly located in the nuclei of myometrial cells, and with the onset of labor, IL-33 expression in the nucleus decreased.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence data in Figure 1.

claim: With the onset of labor, IL-33 expression in the nucleus decreased.
source: Preliminary data showed that IL-33 was mainly located in the nuclei of myometrial cells, and with the onset of labor, IL-33 expression in the nucleus decreased.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and western blot data in Figure 1.

claim: Mast cells responded to the secretion of IL-33 after exposure to allergens.
source: Studies also showed that mast cells responded to the secretion of IL-33 after exposure to the allergens and this affected airway smooth muscle hyper-responsiveness by promoting the contraction and enhancing calcium influx of airway smooth muscle, leading asthma attacks (Bønnelykke et al., 2014; Kaur et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bønnelykke et al., 2014 and Kaur et al., 2015.

claim: IL-33 affected airway smooth muscle hyper-responsiveness by promoting the contraction and enhancing calcium influx of airway smooth muscle, leading asthma attacks.
source: Studies also showed that mast cells responded to the secretion of IL-33 after exposure to the allergens and this affected airway smooth muscle hyper-responsiveness by promoting the contraction and enhancing calcium influx of airway smooth muscle, leading asthma attacks (Bønnelykke et al., 2014; Kaur et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bønnelykke et al., 2014 and Kaur et al., 2015.

claim: IL-33 was found to be effective in alleviating the myocardial endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response caused by myocardial injury.
source: In addition, IL-33 was found to be effective in alleviating the myocardial endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response caused by myocardial injury (Yao et al., 2017; Theoharides et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yao et al., 2017 and Theoharides et al., 2010.

claim: IL-33 was expressed in the nuclei of myometrial cells as shown by immunohistochemistry.
source: Immunohistochemistry with the anti-IL-33 antibody revealed that IL-33 was expressed in the nuclei of myometrial cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The TL and PTL groups showed weak staining of IL-33 in the nuclei of myometrium cells.
source: The TL and PTL groups showed weak staining of IL-33 in the nuclei of myometrium cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Strong nuclear staining of IL-33 was observed in the myometrial cells of TNL and PNL groups.
source: In contrast, strong nuclear staining of IL-33 was observed in the myometrial cells of TNL and PNL groups (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The expression of nuclear IL-33 was more intense in the TNL and PNL groups when compared with TL and PTL groups.
source: It should be noted that the expression of nuclear IL-33 was more intense in the TNL and PNL groups when compared with TL and PTL groups.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There were similar levels of staining in the two no labor groups as well as the two labor groups.
source: There were similar levels of staining in the two no labor groups as well as the two labor groups (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There was no difference in the expression of total IL-33 among all groups.
source: Western blotting analysis revealed that there was no difference in the expression of total IL-33 among all groups.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There were decreased levels of nuclear IL-33 from the TNL to the TL groups.
source: There were decreased levels of nuclear IL-33 from the TNL to the TL groups, which was consistent with the change seem from PNL to PTL.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data of nuclear fractions shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The change in nuclear IL-33 from TNL to TL was consistent with the change from PNL to PTL.
source: There were decreased levels of nuclear IL-33 from the TNL to the TL groups, which was consistent with the change seem from PNL to PTL.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data of nuclear fractions shown in Figure 1C.

claim: mRNA expression of total IL-33 was not different between the different groups.
source: The results of qPCR suggested that mRNA expression of total IL-33 was not different between the different groups (Figure 1C).

claim: Following treatment with LPS, there was a marked decrease in endonuclear IL-33 levels for approximately 3 hr.
source: Following treatment with LPS, there was a marked decrease in endonuclear IL-33 levels for approximately 3 hr and then this increased to above control values by 12 hr, which was higher than that in the control group (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence time course data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Endonuclear IL-33 increased to above control values by 12 hr after LPS treatment.
source: Following treatment with LPS, there was a marked decrease in endonuclear IL-33 levels for approximately 3 hr and then this increased to above control values by 12 hr, which was higher than that in the control group (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence time course data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The expression levels of total IL-33 were reduced within 6 hr of LPS treatment, and then peaked at 12 hr.
source: Western blots confirmed that the expression levels of total IL-33 were reduced within 6 hr, and then peaked at 12 hr.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Nuclear IL-33 reduced with the stimulation by LPS.
source: Western blot analysis showed that nuclear IL-33 reduced with the stimulation by LPS.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data of nuclear fractions shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Nuclear IL-33 levels peaked again at 12 hr after LPS treatment, and were higher than seen in control cells.
source: However, the levels peaked again in the nucli at 12 hr, and were higher than seen in control cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data of nuclear fractions shown in Figure 2B.

claim: LPS induces a time-dependent reduction of IL-33 in the nucleus.
source: This indicates that LPS induces a time-dependent reduction of IL-33 in the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the time course data in Figure 2.

claim: An increase in intracellular calcium levels was observed after LPS stimulation for 0.5–6 hr.
source: After stimulating for 0.5–6 hr, an increase in intracellular calcium levels was observed by using laser confocal microscopy to observe the added intracellular fluorescent probes which were consistent with the calcium channels status (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data using fluo-3AM shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Apparent enhancement in the protein levels of calcium channels proteins, Cav3.1 and Cav3.2, was demonstrated after siRNA-based LPS treatment.
source: Apparent enhancement in the protein levels of calcium channels proteins, Cav3.1 and Cav3.2, was also demonstrated after siRNA-based LPS treatment while siRNA-mediated efficient knockdown of IL-33 was simultaneously observed (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: BAPTA-AM attenuated the expression of LPS-induced COX-2 after 12 hr.
source: The results showed an attenuation in the expression of LPS-induced cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) after 12 hr of preloading cells with BAPTA-AM (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: p-IRE1α and XBP1s in the myocytes of prechelated-based stimulation showed a decreasing trend when compared with cells stimulated by LPS directly.
source: We found that p-IRE1α and XBP1s in the myocytes of prechelated-based stimulation showed a decreasing trend when compared with cells stimulated by LPS directly.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was no apparent alteration in protein levels of GRP78 in prechelated-based stimulation.
source: Furthermore, on the basis that there was no significant difference detected after LPS treatment when directly compared to controls, there was no apparent alteration in protein levels of GRP78 in prechelated-based stimulation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The protein expression of the ER stress‐sensing molecules, p-IRE1α and XBP1s, was significantly increased in the TL and PTL groups when compared with the TNL and PNL groups.
source: As shown in Figure 5A, the protein expression of the ER stress‐sensing molecules, p-IRE1α and XBP1s, was significantly increased in the TL and PTL groups when compared with the TNL and PNL groups.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There was no significant change in GRP78 protein expression among the groups.
source: However, there was no significant change in GRP78 protein expression among the groups.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The mRNA expression of GRP78 had no intergroup differences.
source: qPCR showed that the mRNA expression of GRP78 had no intergroup differences.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: XBP1s mRNA expression was increased in PTL when compared with PNL.
source: However, XBP1s mRNA expression was increased in PTL when compared with PNL, but there was no difference between the TNL and TL groups.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There was no difference in XBP1s mRNA expression between the TNL and TL groups.
source: However, XBP1s mRNA expression was increased in PTL when compared with PNL, but there was no difference between the TNL and TL groups.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The activation of ER stress is a potential mechanism underlying labor.
source: Overall, these findings support the hypothesis that the activation of ER stress is a potential mechanism underlying labor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing increased ER stress markers in labor tissues.

claim: LPS stimulated primary myometrial cells and induced the ER stress response without altering GRP78 protein levels.
source: In order to confirm this, we stimulated primary myometrial cells with LPS and induced the ER stress response without altering GRP78 protein levels.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The expression levels of p-IRE1α and XBP1s reached their peaks at 30 min and 1 hr after LPS treatment, and then decreased to almost the basal levels at 12 hr.
source: We found that the expression levels of p-IRE1α and XBP1s reached their peaks at 30 min and 1 hr, and then decreased to almost the basal levels at 12 hr (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot time course data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: IL-33 knockdown heightened the LPS-induced ER stress response.
source: We next suppressed the expression with IL-33 siRNA in these cells and found that IL-33 knockdown heightened the LPS-induced ER stress response.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: XBP1s and phosphorylated IRE1α protein levels were increased in the IL-33 siRNA group compared to the LPS group.
source: This is shown in Figure 5D and in contrast to the LPS group, XBP1s and phosphorylated IRE1α protein levels were increased in the IL-33 siRNA group.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: COX-2 was upregulated in the IL-33 siRNA group after LPS treatment for 12 hr.
source: COX-2 was upregulated of in the IL-33 siRNA group (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 4μ8C inhibited the expression of COX-2 markedly.
source: The results demonstrated that 4μ8C inhibited the expression of COX-2 markedly (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The expression of phosphorylation of p38/MAPK and NF-κB increased significantly when LPS caused an induction of COX-2 expression, and these peaked after 30 min.
source: We also found the expression of phosphorylation of p38 /mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) increased significantly when LPS caused an induction of COX-2 expression, and these peaked after 30 min (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot time course data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: When siRNA-based LPS stimulation lasted for 1 hr, the protein levels of NF-κB phosphorylation were significantly increased compared to that of the group without IL-33 knockout.
source: Based on the knockdown experiments targeting IL-33 which showed that when siRNA-based LPS stimulation lasted for 1 hr, the protein levels of NF-κB phosphorylation were significantly increased compared to that of the group without IL-33 knockout.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The phosphorylation of p38 was not significantly different within 30 min of LPS stimulus but elevated sharply when the stimulus lasted for 30 min.
source: However, the phosphorylation of p38 was not significantly different within 30 min of LPS stimulus but elevated sharply when the stimulus lasted for 30 min (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: COX-2 expression was significantly reduced when p38 and NF-κB signaling pathway inhibitors, SB-202190 and JSH-23, were added before LPS treatment.
source: In addition, p38 and NF-κB signaling pathway inhibitors, SB-202190 and JSH-23, respectively, were added before LPS treatment, and western blotting analysis showed that COX-2 expression was significantly reduced (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The expression levels of IL-8 and IL-6 in the supernatants of the LPS and siRNA treated cells were increased when compared with the controls.
source: The expression levels of IL-8 and IL-6 in the supernatants of the LPS and siRNA treated cells were increased when compared with the controls.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 8.

claim: More IL-8 and IL-6 were released into the cell supernatants after IL-33 siRNA transfection compared with the LPS group.
source: In addition, in comparison with the LPS group, more IL-8 and IL-6 were released into the cell supernatants after IL-33 siRNA transfection and partial binding of cytoplasmic calcium ions (Figure 8).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 8.

claim: More IL-8 and IL-6 were released into the cell supernatants after partial binding of cytoplasmic calcium ions compared with the LPS group.
source: In addition, in comparison with the LPS group, more IL-8 and IL-6 were released into the cell supernatants after IL-33 siRNA transfection and partial binding of cytoplasmic calcium ions (Figure 8).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 8.

claim: As the myometrium switches from a quiescent to a contractile state, it also undergoes a shift in signaling from anti-inflammatory to proinflammatory pathways.
source: Our current understanding of this process is that as the myometrium switches from a quiescent to a contractile state, it also undergoes a shift in signaling from anti-inflammatory to proinflammatory pathways (Hadley et al., 2018; Shynlova et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hadley et al., 2018 and Shynlova et al., 2020.

claim: IL-33 is composed of a N-terminal nuclear domain and a C-terminal IL-1-like cytokine domain which is mainly localized in the nucleus and binds to histones and chromatin.
source: IL-33 is composed of a N-terminal nuclear domain and a C-terminal IL-1-like cytokine domain which is mainly localized in the nucleus and binds to histones and chromatin (Martin and Martin, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Martin and Martin, 2016 and represents established knowledge about IL-33 structure.

claim: IL-33 plays a dual role, playing a proinflammatory role as an inflammatory cytokine outside the cell as well as participating in the regulation of transcription as a nuclear factor.
source: We proposed that IL-33 plays a dual role, playing a proinflammatory role as an inflammatory cytokine outside the cell as well as participating in the regulation of transcription as a nuclear factor (Carriere et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors, supported by citation to Carriere et al., 2007.

claim: IL-33 has an essential role in pregnancy-related diseases such as recurrent abortion and preeclampsia.
source: Numerous studies have shown that IL-33 had an essential role in pregnancy-related diseases such as recurrent abortion and preeclampsia (Hu et al., 2015; Fock et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hu et al., 2015 and Fock et al., 2013.

claim: In early pregnancy, IL-33 can increase the proliferation and invasion of the decidua.
source: In early pregnancy, IL-33 can increase the proliferation and invasion of the decidua, and decidual macrophage-derived IL-33 is a key factor for placental growth, and its deletion can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes (Sheng et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sheng et al., 2018 and Hu et al., 2014.

claim: Decidual macrophage-derived IL-33 is a key factor for placental growth.
source: In early pregnancy, IL-33 can increase the proliferation and invasion of the decidua, and decidual macrophage-derived IL-33 is a key factor for placental growth, and its deletion can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes (Sheng et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sheng et al., 2018 and Hu et al., 2014.

claim: Deletion of decidual macrophage-derived IL-33 can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes.
source: In early pregnancy, IL-33 can increase the proliferation and invasion of the decidua, and decidual macrophage-derived IL-33 is a key factor for placental growth, and its deletion can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes (Sheng et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sheng et al., 2018 and Hu et al., 2014.

claim: IL-33 expression is reduced in the placenta of preeclamptic patients.
source: Similarly, IL-33 expression is reduced in the placenta of preeclamptic patients, which is a condition that affects placental function by reducing the proliferation, migration, and invasion of trophoblast cells (Chen et al., 2018; Spaans et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2018 and Spaans et al., 2014.

claim: Reduced IL-33 in preeclampsia affects placental function by reducing the proliferation, migration, and invasion of trophoblast cells.
source: Similarly, IL-33 expression is reduced in the placenta of preeclamptic patients, which is a condition that affects placental function by reducing the proliferation, migration, and invasion of trophoblast cells (Chen et al., 2018; Spaans et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2018 and Spaans et al., 2014.

claim: IL-33, a mucosal alarmin, was being sequestered in the nucleus in order to limit its proinflammatory potential.
source: This was consistent with previous studies which showed that IL-33, a mucosal alarmin, was being sequestered in the nucleus in order to limit its proinflammatory potential.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on prior literature about IL-33 function.

claim: IL-33 is released as a warning signal when tissues are damaged following stress or infection such as its release from the nucleus during asthma attack.
source: It was released as a warning signal when tissues were damaged following stress or infection such as its release from the nucleus during asthma attack (Kaur et al., 2015; Pelletier and Savignac, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kaur et al., 2015 and Pelletier and Savignac, 2018.

claim: IL-33 is a dual-function protein that might act both as a cytokine and as an intracellular nuclear factor.
source: Meanwhile, it was reported that IL-33 is a dual-function protein that might act both as a cytokine and as an intracellular nuclear factor (Gautier et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gautier et al., 2016.

claim: LPS stimulation of uterine explants could cause an ER stress response in uterine muscle.
source: Researchers recently found that LPS stimulation of uterine explants could cause an ER stress response in uterine muscle.
evidence: This is based on prior research findings.

claim: Dysregulation of ER homeostasis in uterine smooth muscle might be one of the mechanisms of LPS-induced inflammatory preterm delivery.
source: This led them to hypothesized that dysregulation of ER homeostasis in uterine smooth muscle might be one of the mechanisms of LPS-induced inflammatory preterm delivery (Guzel et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior research, supported by citation to Guzel et al., 2017.

claim: The levels of GRP78, IRE1, and XBP1s in fetal membranes and myometrium were elevated in both TL and PTL when compared with nonlaboring specimens.
source: When compared with nonlaboring specimens, the levels of GRP78, IRE1, and XBP1s in fetal membranes and myometrium were elevated in both TL and PTL (Liong and Lappas, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liong and Lappas, 2014.

claim: The expression of the ER stress response in the uterine smooth muscle was increased during labor when compared to nonlabor tissues.
source: Consistently, the expression of the ER stress response in the uterine smooth muscle was increased during labor when compared to nonlabor tissues.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' own data in Figure 5A showing increased p-IRE1α and XBP1s in labor groups.

claim: GRP78 binds to three prominent ER stress proteins under steady-state conditions: PERK, ATF6, and IRE1α.
source: As a chaperone protein in the ER, GRP78 binds to three prominent ER stress proteins under steady-state conditions. These are PERK and ATF6, which are related to redox reaction and the Golgi apparatus, respectively. An additional protein, IRE1α, is also involved and it is related to inflammatory signals and the repair of misfolded proteins (Ron and Walter, 2007; Oakes and Papa, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ER stress pathways, supported by citations to Ron and Walter, 2007 and Oakes and Papa, 2015.

claim: During the adaptive phase of the ER stress response, the IRE1α–XBP1s pathway is activated.
source: During the adaptive phase of the ER stress response, the IRE1α–XBP1s pathway is activated.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ER stress signaling pathways.

claim: The decrease in nuclear IL-33 prompted the increase of COX-2 expression after LPS stimulation.
source: To explore the potential mechanism of how IL-33 is involved in the process of labor, we transfected siRNA IL-33 into primary myometrial cells, and the decrease in nuclear IL-33 prompted the increase of COX-2 expression after LPS stimulation.
